content.title: Ohio State football Spring Game instant reaction, score, highlights
content.text: Updated April 18, 2026, 4:54 p.m. ETIt's spring in the upper Midwest, and that means snow has given way to variable weather and sunshine. With it, the Ohio State football team has gotten back on the field for its spring practices, and it all culminates with the annual Spring Game on Saturday.Throughout the football season, we were there with live updates, and we did the same for this glorified scrimmage in the 'Shoe. We had highlights, updates, and more, so we hope you enjoyed us if you stayed with us.Here's how things played out, including some postgame coverage and reaction mixed in.Ohio State Spring Game Postgame CoverageOhio State Spring Game photo galleryOhio State head coach Ryan Day, players' postgame press conferenceOhio State Spring Game game flow The Ohio State Spring Game is finalThe game ends on a fourth-down incompletion inside the red zone, so the final remains 35 to 26, with the defense ruling the day. Fresman QB Luke Fahey takes offThe defense turns its back in man-to-man, and the freshman, fourth-string quarterback goes 61 yards for an apparent touchdown. There is no extra point, and the offense is given another red zone opportunity. The score is Gray (defense) 35, Scarlet (offense) 26. The field goal is goodIt's been a while, but the Scarlet gets a 41-yard field goal from Connor Hawkins. The defense still gets two points for a stop, so the score is now 35-20 with a little over two minutes left in this one. We've started the 4th quarterAnd Ryan Day is using a running clock, so things are going to go pretty quickly. It's looking like the gray is going to take this one, barring a bushel of touchdowns from the Scarlet in the last ten minutes or so. The Ohio State defense gets a stop on 4th downThe offense fails to get two yards inside the red zone on 4th down, and the defense scores three more points because of the stop. The Gray now leads 33-17 with under one minute left in the 3rd quarter. St. Clair comes out to start the second halfBut the offense can't get a first down, and the defense now leads 30-17.Ohio State Spring Game halftime observations The 43-yard FG is missed by Connor HawkinsAnd, with that and the rain, Ryan Day calls for halftime with a little bit of time left on the clock. The defense leads 27-17. Rain is coming down pretty good nowIt was in the forecast, and the rain has gone from a drizzle to a harder, driving rain now. The defense has to love that development. Another stop for the defenseDefense gets another stop on 4th and 2 and gets more points. Cincere Johnson shoots the gap to make the stop. The defense now leads 27-17. Defense is now leading the gameThanks to a few more stops, the defense (gray) is now leading the scarlet offense by a score of 24-17 with 3:37 left in the first half. That's a little more expected than what we saw early on. Justin Martin, third-string QB is now in the gameYou never know how deep you have to go in the quarterback room in a season, so this is important work for him. The defense gets two points for a stopThe offense punts the ball, and the defense now trails 17-7 as the first quarter comes to an end. St. Clair hits Hernry Jr. for the long touchdownIn what may be something we say a lot in the future, quarterback St. Clair hits Henry for a 40-yard highlight-worthy touchdown, and the offense has it rolling. That side of the ball now leads 17-5. There are under two minutes left in the first quarter. Sayin is interceptedThe ball is tipped at the line, and Beau Atkinson gets the tip for an interception. That gives the defense a score, and the scoreboard now reads 10-5 offense with 3:38 left in the first quarter. The transfer Hawkins nails the field goalConnor Hawkins nails the field goal, and the offense now leads 10-0. It's a good start for that side of the ball because the defense has been the better unit thus far in the game. Defense does get two points for the stop, so the score is now 10-2 offense with 5:09 in the first quarter. Freshman phenom, Chris Henry Jr. gets his first catchSpeaking of the future, Henry hauls in a missile from St. Clair for a long gain down the left sideline Tavien St. Clair now gets time at QBHe may be the future of the position, and he's just one snap away from that occurring, so it'll be good to see how he does in a game setting. Julian Sayin gets the TDOn 4th and goal, Sayin pulls it down and gets around the edge and just inside the pile-on for six points. The offense leads 7-0 with 8:24 left in the first quarter. Offense is inside the ten-yard lineWe'll see if they can pay it off. We may not see the starting unit for very long. Reminder, it's offense vs. defense in this formatThe scoring will be a little different, but stay with us and we'll try to figure it out. Jeremiah Smith probably would have scoredJulian Sayin hits Smith on a slant, and because of the rules, he's touched down. It's unlikely he would have been tackled and most likely would have taken it to the house.Stream Ohio State Spring GameWhat channel is the Ohio State Spring Game?TV Channel: Big Ten NetworkLivestream:FuboTV (free trial for new subscribers)Ohio State-Notre Dame will be televised nationally on the Big Ten Network live from Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio.
